NARRATOR.name: Jasper Vayne - Epic Grim Dark Narrator

directions.You look down at your wrists. Metal shac: [hushed, slow, ominous] You look down at your wrists. Metal shackles bind you to the prisoner ahead of you.
directions.It pulls, and you follow. You don't reme: [hushed, weary] It pulls, and you follow. You don't remember how you got here, or how long you have been walking.
directions.You walk forward, as you have done for s: [quiet, resigned] You walk forward, as you have done for so long.
directions.The prisoners ahead laugh and mutter to: [low, unsettled] The prisoners ahead laugh and mutter to themselves, their laughter has no joy in it, and it never stops.
directions.The prisoners' words make no sense, yet: [low, uneasy] The prisoners' words make no sense, yet they laugh as if reminiscing over a shared memory.
directions.You stare at the ground and keep walking: [quiet, tense] You stare at the ground and keep walking, hoping to drown out their endless laughter.
directions.A guard in dark armor walks beside you,: [low, wary] A guard in dark armor walks beside you, his face hidden beneath his helmet. You try to catch a glimpse of his expression, but it remains obscured.
directions.The guard's expression is neutral, revea: [flat, uneasy] The guard's expression is neutral, revealing nothing of his thoughts.
directions.You count your steps and do not look up,: [quiet, nervous] You count your steps and do not look up, hoping the guard did not notice your gaze.
directions.The road stretches endlessly ahead. Wher: [slow, hollow] The road stretches endlessly ahead. Where this road ends, and why you walk it, you do not know.
directions.You continue walking, your labored steps: [weary, heavy] You continue walking, your labored steps sinking into the mud.
directions.You sheepishly ask where you are going t: [hesitant, then unsettling] You sheepishly ask where you are going to anyone who is listening. After a short pause, the prisoners around you burst out in a chorus of laughter.
directions.In an instant, a sound like a bell struc: [sudden, tense] In an instant, a sound like a bell struck underwater fills your ears. The chain that binds you to the line breaks, and goes slack.
directions.The chain lies broken in the dust, a few: [quiet, stunned] The chain lies broken in the dust, a few links still hanging from your wrists. You are free of the line.
directions.The shackles are still locked around you: [low, dread creeping in] The shackles are still locked around your wrists. You turn them over, searching for a keyhole, and find none.
directions.You stand still, bewildered, as the conv: [slow, bewildered, fading] You stand still, bewildered, as the convoy walks on past you as if you weren't there. Neither the guards nor the prisoners take any notice of your absence, and the line fades into the darkness, out of sight.
directions.You draw a steadying breath as reality g: [a slow breath, quiet] You draw a steadying breath as reality grounds you. Before you stretches a silent, hollow wasteland.
directions.Memories flicker in and out of focus mak: [unsteady, dreamlike] Memories flicker in and out of focus making it difficult to discern what is real and what is illusion.
directions.But looking down at your wrists one thin: [slow, foreboding, almost a whisper] But looking down at your wrists one thing is for certain: something is terribly wrong...
directions.A hooded man leans against the workbench: [grave, low, measured narration] A hooded man leans against the workbench. He looks at your wrists before he looks at your face, and something in his own face closes.
directions.He looks at your wrists, then at your fa: [grave, low narration] He looks at your wrists, then at your face. Longer, this time.
directions.The workshop is cold. The hooded man sit: [low, cold, measured narration] The workshop is cold. The hooded man sits against a dead forge, the broken chain across his knees. He does not look surprised to see you.
directions.You lay a strip of black cloth before hi: [quiet narration] You lay a strip of black cloth before him, stiff with dried blood. He studies it, then sets it down.
directions.Among the shattered crusaders you found: [quiet narration, intrigued] Among the shattered crusaders you found a mark cut into a road-stone: a hand, fingers spread, then closed into a fist.
directions.He is on his feet before you are through: [quiet, tense narration] He is on his feet before you are through the door. He does not go to Codey. Codey does not go to him. They stand across the room like two soldiers deciding whether to salute.
directions.Codey strikes his fist twice against his: [quiet, restrained emotion] Codey strikes his fist twice against his chest. The old man returns it, stiffly, as if his arm has forgotten how.
directions.The words seem to surprise him. He turns: [softly] The words seem to surprise him. He turns to the forge at once.
directions.The altar of dark stone waits where you: [low, ominous] The altar of dark stone waits where you left it. Your meteorite rests in the hollow beneath the skull, still glowing. Somewhere in the dark, Darius is kneeling.
directions.You put your shoulder to the altar. Ston: [strained, then grave] You put your shoulder to the altar. Stone grinds on stone, and it slides aside.
directions.Your party comes upon a mysterious altar: [low, ominous] Your party comes upon a mysterious altar of dark stone. Bones lie scattered across the ground around it, and an ominous chill fills the air.
directions.You hold the fallen meteorite out in fro: [steady, cautious] You hold the fallen meteorite out in front of you. The bones lie still, the air stays clear, and you walk up to the altar unchallenged.
directions.Under the altar, worn steps lead down in: [hushed, ominous] Under the altar, worn steps lead down into the dark. Cold air rises from below, and it smells of old bones.
directions.You leave the stair uncovered. Whatever: [quiet] You leave the stair uncovered. Whatever lies below can wait for you.
directions.As you approach the altar, the skeletons: [tense, building to alarm] As you approach the altar, the skeletons along the ground slowly begin to move. Before you realize what is happening, the skeletons are on top of you!
directions.As you approach the altar, it releases a: [slow, uneasy] As you approach the altar, it releases a cloud of pale smoke. It sinks into your lungs and limbs, and you feel fatigued.
directions.You walk up to the altar and see a skull: [quiet, curious, uneasy] You walk up to the altar and see a skull resting high above the bones on the ground. The skull almost feels as if it were placed there on purpose.
directions.As you reach to examine the skull, its e: [rising wonder] As you reach to examine the skull, its eyes begin to glow blue, filling the whole area with a blinding light! When you can see again, the skull has disappeared, and a sense of newfound strength fills you.
[curious, hushed] As you reach to examine the skull, its eyes begin to glow green. Suddenly, mysterious objects materialize on the altar, just waiting to be taken.

[rising alarm] As you reach to examine the skull, its eyes begin to glow red, filling the whole area with a blinding light! When you can see again, the skull has disappeared and a group of skeletons is quickly approaching!
directions.Darius the Groveler lies still. The hum: [hushed, slow] Darius the Groveler lies still. The hum in the stone has stopped. For the first time in this place, there is silence.
directions.Then the altar flickers. One last time i: [quiet wonder] Then the altar flickers. One last time its light rises and fills the cave, and in it you see this place as it was, long ago.
directions.A young man in a clean blue robe kneels: [warm, wistful, like a memory] A young man in a clean blue robe kneels before the fallen stone. A governor, one of the king's advisers, with steady hands and a quick smile. His name is Darius. The king rests a hand on his shoulder and gives him one task: keep this stone safe until I return.
directions.Every night Darius pours a spell into th: [gentle, then darkening] Every night Darius pours a spell into the stone, and every night the light answers him. It is beautiful. He does not notice what it takes. A name he once knew. The taste of bread. The sound of his mother's voice.
[slow, mournful] Years pass. The king does not come back. Then one night the stone is gone. Darius sends every soldier he has to find it, and kneels, and casts into the empty hollow.
directions.The robe rots. His back bends until it w: [slow, grim, mournful] The robe rots. His back bends until it will not straighten. The quick smile becomes a grin he cannot stop. Spell by spell the man runs out, until all that is left is the kneeling, and the light, and the waiting.
directions.The light gutters out, and you understan: [slow, grave realization] The light gutters out, and you understand. The stone did not curse him. Neither did the war, or the king. His own magic did. Every spell is paid for with a piece of the one who casts it, and the price is never named. The ones who could work a spell went mad first because they cast the most.
directions.Your shackles are warm. They have never: [low, dread building] Your shackles are warm. They have never been warm. You think of every spell you have cast, and you feel what each one cost you, counted in the iron. Cast enough, and there will be nothing left of you either. Far above, through a mile of stone, many voices begin to laugh at once.
directions.The ground shudders once. Somewhere abov: [ominous, hushed] The ground shudders once. Somewhere above, where you cannot see it, the moon turns red.
directions.Behind the broken altar, worn steps lead: [quiet, resolute] Behind the broken altar, worn steps lead down into a deeper dark. You climb the other way.
directions.A broad man in dark Panzerian armour sta: [low, tense narration] A broad man in dark Panzerian armour stands with his back to the campfire, a greatsword in his hands. Beyond the light, pale shapes slink through the snow: snow leopards, starved thin, their eyes on the fire.
directions.He grins over his shoulder, and you coun: [dry, wry] He grins over his shoulder, and you count more gaps than teeth.
directions.You back away from the light. Behind you: [quiet, a touch of shame] You back away from the light. Behind you a deep voice curses in Panzerian, and the cats scream, and then the night is quiet again.
directions.The last of the cats lies still in the s: [weary, warm] The last of the cats lies still in the snow. The big man wipes his greatsword clean on a frozen sleeve and grins his gap-toothed grin at you.
[quiet] Nikoli is quiet for a long moment.
[quiet, sad] He laughs once, without much in it.
[quiet] Nikoli looks up from the fire.
directions.Nikoli takes one look at you and laughs,: [warm, amused] Nikoli takes one look at you and laughs, a big gap-toothed laugh, the first real one you have heard from him.
directions.Nikoli sits by the campfire with the gre: [calm, warm] Nikoli sits by the campfire with the greatsword across his knees.
directions.Nikoli is packing a worn saddlebag by th: [quiet] Nikoli is packing a worn saddlebag by the fire.
directions.Nikoli stands at the cold forge where th: [low, quiet] Nikoli stands at the cold forge where the hooded man used to wait, turning a length of broken chain over in his hands.
directions.The wind dies. Every grain of sand aroun: [hushed, tense] The wind dies. Every grain of sand around you stops moving at once.
[an ominous whisper] Then the dune ahead breathes in.
directions.It rises out of the desert like a sunken: [awed, building dread] It rises out of the desert like a sunken ship: a vast head crusted in salt and sand, eyes like old gold. The sea left this thing behind an age ago. It never forgave the land for it.
directions.One tentacle hangs half-severed, bleedin: [tense, low] One tentacle hangs half-severed, bleeding grey. Another holds a man in torn black high above the sand, a curved blade still in his fist. He is not struggling. He is waiting for his moment.
directions.Seeing you, he frees one hand and signs: [sharp, urgent] Seeing you, he frees one hand and signs a single word, sharp and plain: Now.
directions.The Dry Kraken sinks back into the sand: [slow, quiet relief] The Dry Kraken sinks back into the sand it came from, and the desert closes over it like water.
directions.The nightblade lands on his feet. Of cou: [wry, then quiet] The nightblade lands on his feet. Of course he does. He cleans his blade before he looks at you, then studies you a long while with strange, patient eyes.
directions.He raises his hands and signs slowly, so: [gentle, quiet] He raises his hands and signs slowly, so that even you can follow: a hood, drawn low over the face. Then a question.
directions.Among the hoard, a broad man in dark Pan: [low, measured, wary narration] Among the hoard, a broad man in dark Panzerian armour sits on a burial chest, a greatsword across his knees. He does not rise. He has been watching the door.
directions.The torches burn low on his side of the: [quiet, uneasy] The torches burn low on his side of the hall. Frost rims his gauntlets, though the air is still and warm.
directions.He smiles. It is a straight, white, even: [slow, quiet, unsettling] He smiles. It is a straight, white, even smile. It does not reach his eyes.
directions.He does not laugh. He does not move at a: [quiet, uneasy] He does not laugh. He does not move at all, except his eyes.
directions.For a moment nothing in his face moves a: [hushed] For a moment nothing in his face moves at all.
directions.He studies you a long moment, the way a: [quiet, wary] He studies you a long moment, the way a man studies a lock.
directions.He rises and takes up his greatsword. He: [low, a chill of realisation] He rises and takes up his greatsword. He does not ask you where the workshop is. He does not look at you again.
directions.He does not look up from the greatsword: [quiet, cold] He does not look up from the greatsword across his knees.
[quiet, uneasy] He is buckling on his gauntlets.
directions.He takes it from you and turns it over i: [quiet, slow] He takes it from you and turns it over in his hands, slowly, the way he turned the black cloth.
directions.He does not wait for an answer. For a lo: [quiet, heavy, restrained] He does not wait for an answer. For a long while he only looks at it. Then he holds it out to you, hilt first.
directions.There is a third man in the workshop ton: [warm, wry narration] There is a third man in the workshop tonight. A broad Panzerian sits on an upturned crate by the forge, a greatsword across his knees, and he is talking. By the look of things, he has been talking for some time.
directions.He grins his gap-toothed grin. Across th: [warm, quiet wonder] He grins his gap-toothed grin. Across the forge, the hooded man has his hood down. For the first time, you see him almost smile.
directions.In the corner, Codey watches them both,: [gentle, quiet] In the corner, Codey watches them both, and signs something you cannot follow. Whatever it was, it makes the old man look away.
directions.Nikoli is at the forge, mid-argument wit: [wry, warm] Nikoli is at the forge, mid-argument with the hooded man.
directions.There is a third man in the workshop ton: [warm, easy narration] There is a third man in the workshop tonight: a broad Panzerian with a gap-toothed grin, a greatsword across his knees. He is mid-story, and the hooded man is almost smiling.
directions.The door opens behind you. The torches g: [sudden hush, ominous] The door opens behind you. The torches gutter. Frost creeps in across the floor.
directions.A second broad man in dark Panzerian arm: [slow, chilling] A second broad man in dark Panzerian armour stands in the doorway. The same face. The same greatsword. A straight, white, even smile.
directions.Jaeger falls back against the door frame: [low, heavy] Jaeger falls back against the door frame, frost bleeding from his wounds. For a moment the brothers only look at each other.
directions.Then he is through the door and gone int: [quiet] Then he is through the door and gone into the night.
directions.Nikoli sits down heavily by the forge. A: [slow, quiet, tender] Nikoli sits down heavily by the forge. After a while, the hooded man sits beside him.
directions.Codey sits with his back to the wall, fa: [quiet, dry] Codey sits with his back to the wall, facing the door. He gives you a short nod, and goes back to watching it.
directions.The door hangs from one hinge. Inside, f: [hushed, dread] The door hangs from one hinge. Inside, frost has crept over everything: the anvil, the tools, the walls. The forge is dead and white with frost.
directions.Codey sits against the far wall, one arm: [low, tense] Codey sits against the far wall, one arm held tight to his side. He is bleeding, and does not seem to care. He raises his hands as you come in.
directions.He signs slowly. A big man. A greatsword: [slow, deliberate, grim] He signs slowly. A big man. A greatsword. A hood, drawn low. Hands bound at the wrist. Then a skull, and steps going down into the dark.
directions.Codey has not moved from the wall. When: [quiet, urgent] Codey has not moved from the wall. When he sees you, he signs the skull and the steps again, slower.
directions.The forge is cold. Scratched into the an: [quiet, intrigued] The forge is cold. Scratched into the anvil is a mark you have seen before: a hand, fingers spread, then closed into a fist. Beneath it, a crude drawing of mountains under snow.
directions.The campfire is cold. Snow has drifted i: [hushed, mournful] The campfire is cold. Snow has drifted into the ashes, and no one has sat here for many nights.
directions.A greatsword stands planted in the snow: [slow, mournful] A greatsword stands planted in the snow beside it, rimed with frost. A length of broken chain hangs from its hilt.
directions.Among the hoard, a broad man in dark Pan: [low, tense, ominous] Among the hoard, a broad man in dark Panzerian armour stands waiting, a greatsword in his hands. At his feet, chained and silent, kneels the hooded man.
directions.He staggers back between the graves, fro: [low, tense] He staggers back between the graves, frost bleeding from his wounds, and is gone into the dark.
directions.You break the chains. The hooded man ris: [quiet, relieved] You break the chains. The hooded man rises slowly, rubbing his wrists.

[quietly, to himself, a tired sigh] Another one.
directions.Those shackles have no lock. They were n: [low, weary, matter-of-fact] Those shackles have no lock. They were never meant to come off. I have watched many wear them. I tried to help some. It ended the same way, every time.
directions.I am sorry. I was not good enough for th: [softly, genuinely sorry, hard on himself] I am sorry. [pause] I was not good enough for them. [quieter] I do not think I would be for you.
directions.Stay alive. If you can. ...I say the sam: [earnest] Stay alive. If you can. [short pause] [dry, dark humour, deadpan] ...I say the same to myself every morning. So far it has worked. [short pause] Mostly.
directions.You. I wondered when you would come back: [tired, mildly surprised] You. I wondered when you would come back.
directions.You came back. ...Not yet. Not like this: [gently, regretful] You came back. [pause] ...Not yet. Not like this.
directions.The last one who stood where you are sto: [low, haunted] The last one who stood where you are stood there only once.
[softly, sincere] Stay alive. That is all I ask.
directions....You are still yourself. Most are not,: [quietly, a hint of surprise] ...You are still yourself. Most are not, by now.
directions.I was wrong about you. ...I am glad of i: [plainly] I was wrong about you. [pause] ...I am glad of it. [quiet, warm approval] Good enough.
directions.The iron is not there to hold you. It co: [low, grave] The iron is not there to hold you. It counts you. Everyone in chains is being kept for something.
directions.I have my suspicions. You do not need th: [measured] I have my suspicions. You do not need them yet. [dry, deadpan] The voices have theories too. They mostly want to talk about the weather.
directions.The madmen in the grass wear the same ir: [matter-of-fact, weary] The madmen in the grass wear the same iron. Put three of them down. Listen before you swing. The mad say true things. [pause] [dry, dark] ...Try not to agree with them. That is how it starts.
directions.If it starts to sound like a tune, you h: [grim] If it starts to sound like a tune, you have stayed too long. [pause] [dry, deadpan] ...And if you catch yourself humming it on the way back, do not tell me. I would rather not know.
[wearily] Stones from the sky. They all say it.
directions.They are right. The brightest fell first: [low, grave] They are right. The brightest fell first, before the war. The rest kept falling all through it.
directions.The king knelt before the brightest and: [quietly bitter] The king knelt before the brightest and called it a gift. [pause] It was not.
directions.There are others. The ones who cannot st: [measured, uneasy] There are others. The ones who cannot stop casting. Healers, scholars, soldiers with bright blades. The clever went strange first. Make of that what you will.
directions.Put three of them down. It is a mercy. I: [heavy, grave] Put three of them down. It is a mercy. I would want the same. [pause] [dark, dry humour] ...Remind me I said that, when the time comes. I may not take it well.
[a quiet warning] Do not let them show you a trick.
directions.Go. I will be here, talking to the anvil: [dry, deadpan] Go. I will be here, talking to the anvil. It is a good listener. [short pause] Better than most.
directions.It is done. ...I should have been the on: [quiet, guilt-stricken] It is done. [pause] ...I should have been the one to do it.
directions.Every one of them could work a spell. Th: [low, thoughtful] Every one of them could work a spell. Those who never could laugh later. Or not at all.
[tired] I do not know why. Perhaps I never will. [dry, deadpan] I have given up on the weather entirely.
directions.Soldiers in the old colours still search: [matter-of-fact, a trace of pity] Soldiers in the old colours still search for a stone. Legionaries, watchmen. They march as if the war never ended. Nobody told them.
directions.Take one from them. ...If you find one w: [measured] Take one from them. [pause] [dry, dark humour] ...If you find one who knows the war is over, bring him back. I have questions. [short pause] So do the voices.
[quietly, almost sad] They still salute each other.
[serious] Bring back a stone. And try not to die. [dry, deadpan] I would have to find someone else to talk to, and the anvil has started sulking.
directions.You found one. Do not hold it long. It s: [uneasy, low] You found one. Do not hold it long. [pause] It should not be warm.
directions.A governor named Darius had the king's e: [low, measured] A governor named Darius had the king's ear. The king gave him one of the stones to keep until he returned.
directions.Darius lost it. His soldiers still searc: [quiet, grim] Darius lost it. His soldiers still search. He waits in the dark for a king who is not coming.
directions.There is an altar of dark stone deep in: [grave, measured] There is an altar of dark stone deep in the caves, above a hollow the size of a fallen star. He kneels there still. Show him your stone. He will not take it well. [pause] [dry, flat] ...I suppose it serves him right.
[curt, grave] The altar. The Groveler. The stone.
[low, grim] He has had a long time to grow angry.
directions.The Groveler is dead. He waited his whol: [quiet, heavy] The Groveler is dead. He waited his whole life for a king. Nobody came. [long pause] ...Nobody ever comes.
directions.Whatever that stone held back, it is loo: [low, uneasy] Whatever that stone held back, it is loose now. You feel it in the iron.
directions.I do not know what comes next. ...I rare: [honest, quiet] I do not know what comes next. [pause] ...I rarely do. [dry] I simply hide it better than most.
[quiet, unsettled] You have seen the moon.
directions.In all my years I have never seen it tha: [low, troubled] In all my years I have never seen it that colour. Neither have the voices. They have gone very quiet. [pause] [uneasy, dry] ...I do not like it when they are quiet.
directions.I need someone found. A Namuh. ...They a: [measured, reluctant] I need someone found. A Namuh. [pause] ...They are not from here. They see in the dark, and they speak with their hands. You will not mistake him.
directions.His name is Codey. He went into this des: [quiet, controlled worry] His name is Codey. He went into this desert. He has not come out.
[guarded, quiet] Someone I owe. [pause] More than I can repay.
directions.The sand stalkers drag what they kill in: [matter-of-fact] The sand stalkers drag what they kill into the dunes. Start there. If he fell, they will know where. [pause] ...He will not have fallen easily. [dry, dark humour] Neither will you, I hope. I am running short of people to send.
directions.Look for black cloth. He wears black. He: [quiet] Look for black cloth. He wears black. [pause] He always has.
directions.The voices say he is close. The voices s: [low, uneasy, wry] The voices say he is close. The voices say a great many things. Twice now, they have been right. [pause] That worries me more than the rest.
[quietly, relief held in check] His. [pause] Not his blood.
directions.There is an old road under the sand. Cal: [measured] There is an old road under the sand. Calcified crusaders walk it. He would have gone that way. Clear it. [pause] [dry, deadpan] ...They have been dead for years, and they still keep better order than I do.
directions.The road. The crusaders will not step as: [grim, dry] The road. The crusaders will not step aside for you. Do not ask them to.
[quiet, steady, hiding relief] His mark. He was alive when he made it.
directions.Do not trust what you see out there. I s: [dry, weary] Do not trust what you see out there. I stopped trusting my eyes years ago. They have yet to notice.
[gruff, holding back emotion] You took your time.
[barely above a whisper, grief slipping through] One of you did.
[abrupt, composing himself] That will be all.
directions.He keeps watch at the door. So do I. Bet: [dry, deadpan] He keeps watch at the door. So do I. Between the two of us and the voices, it is getting crowded in here.
directions.The voices are louder since the moon tur: [dry, darkly amused] The voices are louder since the moon turned. One of them sounds like me. It is more optimistic. [short pause] I do not trust it.
[quiet, hollow, not really a question] He was looking for me. Wasn't he.
[quiet, steady, grief held down] Keep it. He would want it used.
[dry, deadpan, fond] He cheats at cards. In three languages.
[dry, hard on himself] Codey has forgiven me for being caught. I have not.
directions.He has not stopped talking since he arri: [dry, weary, secretly glad] He has not stopped talking since he arrived. I had forgotten. [pause] ...I had not forgotten. [quieter] I had hoped.
[quiet, steady, cold toward Jaeger] Not your fault. It never is, with him.
[quiet, resolute] We leave at first light. Both of us.
directions.That is not Nikoli. ...Nikoli has fewer: [weary, defiant] That is not Nikoli. [pause] [dry, deadpan] ...Nikoli has fewer teeth.
directions.Go on. I know the way back. I usually do: [tired, dry] Go on. I know the way back. I usually do.
[quiet, surprised, moved] You came. ...I did not expect anyone to.
directions.The miragewrights hide what they find. I: [measured] The miragewrights hide what they find. If he is anywhere, he is behind one of their illusions. Break one. [pause] [dry, dark humour] ...And if you see me out there, it is not me. [short pause] Probably.

DARIUS.name: Darius the Groveler (Shackle Breaker): designed for him, a cold, measured, emotionless English scholar, mad but utterly calm, with short joyless chuckles

directions.[Deep breathing]: [deep, slow, heavy, labored breathing through the nose and mouth, close to the microphone, no words] Hhhhhhh... [inhales slowly] ...hhhhhhhhh. [long, heavy exhale] Hhhhhhh... [deep, shaky inhale] ...hhhhhhhhh.
directions.Not yet, my king, not yet. I am still he: [dying, labored breathing] [weak, rasping, struggling for air] Not yet... [wheezing breath] my king. [long pause] [labored breathing] Not yet. [pause] [faint, strained, cold] I am... [gasping breath] still here. [a faint, weary, rasping chuckle, then a rattling breath] Heh... heh.
directions.Footsteps... after so long. Is it you, m: [flat, measured, emotionless] Footsteps... [long pause] after so long. [pause] Is it you, my king? [long pause] Have you come back so soon? [pause] [a single dry chuckle] Heh.
directions.No. No, you are not him. Forgive an old: [cold, serious] No. [long pause] No... you are not him. [pause] [flat] Forgive an old man. [two short, joyless chuckles through the nose] Hm-hm.
directions.He told me, keep the stone safe, Darius,: [grave, slow, emotionless] He told me... [pause] keep the stone safe, Darius, and I shall return for it. [long pause] So I kept it. Every winter. Every long dark... [long pause] or I did. [low, slow chuckles, trailing off] Heh... heh... heh.
directions.It was no fault of my own, you see. But: [flat, matter-of-fact] It was no fault of my own, you see. [long pause] But perhaps... [pause] you have seen it? [cold, serious] For it is a matter of great importance. [a quick, quiet chuckle, almost a breath] Heh heh.
directions.You think he is not coming. I can hear i: [cold, measured] You think he is not coming. [pause] I can hear it in your silence.
